question:
A 64-year-old woman, gravida 3, para 3, visits the outpatient clinic due to involuntary urine leakage.
She reports that the first episode occurred two weeks ago while lifting weights at the gym, and
subsequent episodes happened during forceful laughing and briefly choking on food. She mentions her
youngest child was delivered via cesarean section, and she underwent a hysterectomy five years ago.
Her hypertension and diabetes are well managed with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and
metformin. She is sexually active with her husband and does not use contraception. She denies
experiencing urine leakage during sleep. Physical examination reveals a relaxed anterior vaginal wall,
and neurological examination is normal. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
Answer Choices: (A) Offering patient education about Kegel exercises (B) Obtaining urodynamic
testing (C) Monitoring postvoid residual (D) Recommending pessary placement (E) Performing a
bladder stress test (F) Initiating anticholinergic therapy (G) Ordering a pelvic MRI to assess for
structural abnormalities (H) Referring to physical therapy for pelvic floor strengthening (I) Performing
urethropexy (J) Performing cystoscopy to evaluate for bladder pathology
 A. Performing urethropexy
B. Ordering a pelvic MRI to assess for structural abnormalities
C. Performing a bladder stress test

D. Performing cystoscopy to evaluate for bladder pathology
E. Referring to physical therapy for pelvic floor strengthening
F. Monitoring postvoid residual
G. Obtaining urodynamic testing
H. Initiating anticholinergic therapy
I. Offering patient education about Kegel exercises
J. Recommending pessary placement
